records.question: Which states have made gold money or put bitcoin in a state reserve, and when does each take effect?
records.answer: Gold, yes; bitcoin, not as money. Florida's gold-and-silver legal-tender law took effect July 1, 2026; in Texas, the law makes gold and silver specie legal tender from September 1, 2026, and the state's electronic gold currency may start no sooner than May 1, 2027. Louisiana (June 11, 2025, with a gold-payment registry added June 23, 2026) and Missouri (July 10, 2025) signed gold legal-tender laws whose start dates are not in the record. For bitcoin the rows show reserves, not money: New Hampshire and Arizona passed reserve laws in May 2025, Texas made the first state purchase on November 20, 2025, and Wisconsin's pension sold its stake. Every row is a reconstructed summary without an official link.

records.question: Which banks have used Swift's blockchain ledger, and for what?
records.answer: Swift lists 17 banks for its blockchain ledger. 8 of them appear in 6 transactions the banks themselves published, which they call live pilots. Swift says most of the 17 have transacted, so some have not been named.

records.question: What journal entries does each party book in a tokenized trade?
records.answer: The entries follow the economic object, not the technology. At each step only the parties whose own books hold the cash, the security or the claim debit or credit anything; a token, a chain or a software provider books nothing by itself. The cards below print every entry, step by step.

records.question: When must U.S. Treasury trades be centrally cleared, and which clearinghouses can do it?
records.answer: Under the SEC rule adopted December 13, 2023, eligible secondary-market Treasury cash trades must be centrally cleared by December 31, 2026, and repo by June 30, 2027; the SEC said in February 2025 it does not intend further extensions. Three clearinghouses are registered to do it: FICC (DTCC's subsidiary, the incumbent), CME Securities Clearing (registered December 1, 2025; its launch moved from Q2 to 'later in 2026') and ICE Clear Credit (its Treasury business approved January 30, 2026). The mandate does not apply to the Fed's own operations; clearing those is still only a proposal.

records.question: What changes in central-bank digital money does the Library record?
records.answer: The world record holds 25 dated moves on central-bank digital money in 10 regions, May 13, 2025 to July 1, 2026. It records moves, not a status, so each region below shows its latest move. Only two currencies have a stated status in a package: Japan's possible retail CBDC is 'pilot; not authorized' (September 15, 2026), and the UK digital pound is at grade M1, 'design decision pending' (September 14, 2026); a May 1, 2026 news report says it may be suspended instead, which is disputed and shown with both readings.

records.question: Where is gold moving as money?
records.answer: The world record holds 16 dated gold and reserve moves in 9 regions, January 30, 2025 to September 4, 2026. The newest that is not a social post: the PBoC reports its twentieth straight month of gold buying — 14.93 tonnes in June, the biggest monthly add since 2023, holdings near 2,346 tonnes. (China, July 7, 2026). Tonnages appear only inside each record's text; the master has no buy, sell or tonnage column.

records.question: How do the IMF, the World Bank bodies and the BIS fit together, and where does the Fed connect?
records.answer: Treasury speaks for the U.S. at the IMF and the five World Bank Group bodies (IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID); the Fed Board is the U.S. member of the BIS. The Fed touches them at 5 points: U.S. policy seat; depositary and fiscal agent; SDR certificate chain; IMF surveillance; BIS membership. None of these gives the IMF or the Bank a say in Fed policy, or the Fed a vote inside them. Treasury's October 14, 2026 statement is a U.S. position, not yet a rule change at any of the institutions.

records.question: How could the U.S. leave each international organization?
records.answer: Each of the 27 bodies has its own exit route. Where the founding text names a period, it runs from immediately (Board of Peace) and on receipt of notice (International Monetary Fund) to 90 days (Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons), six months (World Trade Organization, World Intellectual Property Organization), one year (NATO, OECD, International Civil Aviation Organization, International Maritime Organization, International Telecommunication Union) and two years (Organization of American States). For NATO the record adds: 'U.S. domestic statute requires Senate or Congress route'. 3 name a notice route without a period in the record (International Atomic Energy Agency, World Bank Group, ITER). 6 have no simple withdrawal clause (the United Nations Charter has none) and 4 are not memberships the U.S. could leave. 3 exits already carry a date: World Health Organization, UNESCO, Paris Agreement; the WHO exit, stated effective January 22, 2026, is disputed.

records.question: Is anything replacing the international bodies the U.S. is leaving?
records.answer: Not wholesale: the registry counts 0 wholesale replacements among the 27 bodies (as of October 4, 2026). 17 bodies still do their job with no successor. 4 were left or cut with no successor at all: UN Human Rights Council, UNRWA, UNESCO, Paris Agreement. Only 3 show a changed default route, each for one bounded job: U.S. foreign health aid now goes through the America First Global Health Strategy bilateral network (the WHO's universal functions are retained); WTO appeals for participating non-U.S. Members go through the MPIA; and a U.S. side-by-side tax regime sits inside the OECD. Two pieces of new machinery exist (Artemis Accords, Board of Peace), and Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science is doctrine only. The Board of Peace's Gaza field handoff was incomplete in September 2026.

records.question: Japan: which digital-money projects are at what stage?
records.answer: On the Japan money map (as of September 15, 2026), 7 digital-money projects: DCJPY: bounded field test, JPYSC trust stablecoin: live, closed loop, Possible retail CBDC: pilot; not authorized, Project Agorá: controlled real-value test, Swift shared ledger: controlled initial use preparing, Indonesia–Japan QR corridor: production, Retired JGB–HKD DvP adapter: retired. Most still return to an existing bank, trust or Bank of Japan record; a retail CBDC has not been issued. The project map omits a reserve limit; the full saved Japan guide says up to half of issuance may move into qualifying short sovereign securities or term deposits.
